specification_compliance: I12 (r8): the primary path raises when a page text layer cannot be read. _empty_text_pages raises VerticalTextError on a per-page get_text failure (addons/intelligence/app/extractors/pdf.py:316-326). A fitz.open failure during recovery also raises it (pdf.py:287-294). These errors are not swallowed into the fitz fallback, because PdfExtractor.extract does not catch them (pdf.py:184-189).
I12 fallback extractor: _fitz_chunks raises VerticalTextError on a page get_text failure (pdf.py:607-615) instead of skipping the page.

I12 indexing: _extract_file_content re-raises VerticalTextError (addons/intelligence/app/workers/metadata.py:151-152). The indexing function returns False before any DB write (metadata.py:394-401), so existing searchable and section data are kept, text_indexed is not set, and the task stays retryable.

I12 document read: _pdf_page raises VerticalTextError when the text layer read fails (addons/intelligence/app/document_text.py:196-203). The router turns any exception other than Busy into an error response (addons/intelligence/app/routers/document_text.py:94) and does not return partial text.
I8: every PyMuPDF call I traced in the extractor runs inside PYMUPDF_LOCK. This covers extract (pdf.py:184) and _pdf_units (document_text.py:147-152).
potential_unspecified_behavior: _empty_text_pages still returns a partial or empty scanned set when fitz.open itself fails (pdf.py:327-328). The primary path then raises at the second fitz.open (pdf.py:288-294), so I saw no silent success. This depends on the second open also failing.
regression_risks: _extract_with_fitz_fallback still returns an empty fallback result when fitz.open fails (pdf.py:574-577). This is pre-existing behaviour, and it means an unopenable PDF is indexed as empty rather than kept retryable. I12 covers only the page text-layer read, so this is not a violation.
